boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, map-listed destinations on corridors around Regis University, each paired with one documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Sheridan Boulevard — Berkeley Lake Park
cards.subtitle: Berkeley Lake Park beside Sheridan Boulevard
cards.notes: Use the Sheridan Boulevard edge to reach the named lake park; the city bike map identifies Berkeley Lake in this northwest Denver area.
cards.short_summary: A named lake destination on the Sheridan Boulevard side of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver’s 2023 bike map labels Berkeley Lake near Sheridan Boulevard and Regis University.
cards.access_notes: Verify conditions and any site-specific rules before visiting.

cards.title: Sheridan Boulevard — Inspiration Point Park
cards.subtitle: Inspiration Point Park beside Sheridan Boulevard
cards.notes: Follow the Sheridan Boulevard corridor to the named park; Denver’s bike map places Inspiration Point Park northwest of Regis.
cards.short_summary: A documented park stop along the Sheridan Boulevard corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver’s 2023 bike map labels Inspiration Point Park near Sheridan Boulevard and Regis University.
cards.access_notes: Verify conditions and any site-specific rules before visiting.

cards.title: West 50th Avenue — Clear Creek Trail
cards.subtitle: Clear Creek Trail at the West 50th Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the West 50th Avenue area as a connection point for the named Clear Creek Trail shown immediately north of the campus area.
cards.short_summary: A mapped trail connection in the West 50th Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver’s 2023 bike map labels Clear Creek Trail near West 50th Avenue and Regis University.
cards.access_notes: Use only open trail sections and follow posted trail guidance.

cards.title: Lowell Boulevard — Rocky Mountain Lake Park
cards.subtitle: Rocky Mountain Lake Park beside Lowell Boulevard
cards.notes: Head south on Lowell Boulevard to the named park; Denver’s park map marks a playground, restroom, picnic area, and horseshoe pit there.
cards.short_summary: A city-mapped park destination on Lowell Boulevard.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver’s Rocky Mountain Lake Park map identifies the park beside N. Lowell Boulevard and marks a playground, restroom, picnic area, and horseshoe pit.
cards.source_title: Rocky Mountain Lake Park ParkArt Map
cards.access_notes: Check posted park rules and current facility availability.

cards.title: West 46th Avenue — Chaffee Park
cards.subtitle: Chaffee Park by the West 46th Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Take West 46th Avenue toward Tejon Street for Chaffee Park; the official historic-markers guide locates the park between 44th and 45th streets.
cards.short_summary: A named historic park reached from the West 46th Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Colorado’s guide to Denver historic markers locates Chaffee Park from 44th to 45th Streets, between Tejon and Shoshone.
cards.source_title: Denver's Historic Markers, Memorials, Statues and Parks
cards.access_notes: Check posted park rules and current facility availability.

cards.title: Zuni Street — 51st & Zuni Park
cards.subtitle: 51st & Zuni Park on the Zuni Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Zuni Street to reach the named 51st & Zuni Park; Denver’s youth-sports location list identifies it for baseball and softball.
cards.short_summary: A named recreation destination on the Zuni Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver Parks and Recreation’s youth-sports site lists 51st & Zuni Park as a baseball/softball location.
cards.access_notes: Athletic-field access may be scheduled; observe posted site rules.

cards.title: Tennyson Street — Cesar E. Chavez Park
cards.subtitle: Cesar E. Chavez Park on Tennyson Street
cards.notes: Travel the Tennyson Street corridor to this named park; the city’s current court-improvement project includes its basketball court.
cards.short_summary: A Tennyson Street park with a documented city improvement project.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver Parks and Recreation lists Cesar Chavez Park among parks receiving basketball-court improvements.
cards.access_notes: Construction or court access can change; consult current park signage.

cards.title: Tennyson Street — Berkeley Park
cards.subtitle: Berkeley Park on the Tennyson Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Tennyson Street for the named Berkeley Park; Denver Parks and Recreation lists it in a current basketball-court accessibility project.
cards.short_summary: A documented Berkeley park destination on Tennyson Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver Parks and Recreation lists Berkeley Park among parks receiving basketball-court improvements.
cards.access_notes: Construction or court access can change; consult current park signage.

cards.title: West Dunkeld Place — Ashland Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Ashland Recreation Center on West Dunkeld Place
cards.notes: Use West Dunkeld Place to locate Ashland Recreation Center; Denver’s recreation-service page lists the center and its current contact number.
cards.short_summary: A named public recreation-center destination by West Dunkeld Place.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver Parks and Recreation lists Ashland Recreation Center and provides its direct contact number.
cards.access_notes: Contact the center for current programs, admission, and facility access.

cards.title: South Platte River Trail — Carpio Sanguinette Park
cards.subtitle: Carpio Sanguinette Park on the South Platte River Trail corridor
cards.notes: Use the South Platte River Trail corridor to identify Carpio Sanguinette Park; Denver’s Adopt a Trail page names it as a trail-segment endpoint.
cards.short_summary: A named trail-adjacent park documented by Denver’s trail program.
cards.evidence_claim: Denver’s Adopt a Trail page states that South Platte Trail adoptable segments run between Carpio Sanguinette Park and W. 104th Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Use only open trail sections and follow posted trail guidance.
